The comment at settings.py:73-76 explicitly anticipates this class of failure.
- products/review_hog/frontend/CodeReviewScene.tsx:1066-1067: the sole consumer renders `!settings.stamphog_connected && !settings.stamphog_review_inbox_prs` as disabled with the copy "Connect a repository to Stamphog first. Stamphog is not set up for this project yet." For a project that is fully synced, that sentence is false during the outage window.
Blast radius is narrow: the already-on switch stays interactive (tsx:1064-1066 comment), so only the off→on path is blocked, the state self-corrects when the breaker closes, and the fix is a one-line copy reword. No tests cover the exception path (test_settings_api.py only covers the four repo-config states).
votes.refutation: Attempted refutations: (1) Looked for a guard that distinguishes "read failed" from "not connected" -- none exists; the serializer returns a plain bool and the help_text has no unknown state. (2) Looked for a second frontend signal that could soften the copy -- `stamphog_connected` has exactly one consumer (CodeReviewScene.tsx:1066), and the copy is unconditional on a False value. (3) Checked whether the trigger is unreachable -- the stamphog DB is a product DB on the fail-open engine, so `CircuitOpenError` and ordinary `OperationalError` both flow into the broad catch; the code comment itself names this scenario. (4) Checked whether the disabled state alone is the intended, documented degradation -- it is (settings.py:75-76), which is why the finding is only a copy-accuracy issue, not a behavior bug: disabling the enable path when connectivity cannot be verified is defensible; only the wording asserts a fact the backend does not know. That leaves a real but minor user-facing inaccuracy in a degraded path, matching `consider`.

votes.evidence:
Trigger is reachable in production configuration:
- `products/db_routing.yaml:2-3` routes app_label `stamphog` to a separate `stamphog` product database; `products/stamphog/backend/models.py:15,21` confirms `StamphogRepoConfig` is a `ProductTeamModel` on that DB.
- `posthog/settings/data_stores.py:176-179` sets `PRODUCT_DB_FAIL_OPEN_ENGINE = "posthog.db_backends.failopen"` and `PRODUCT_DB_CIRCUIT_BREAKER_ENABLED` defaults to `not TEST`, i.e. on in prod; lines 213-223 assign that engine to both `stamphog_db_writer` and `stamphog_db_reader` with `connect_timeout = 3`.
- `posthog/db_backends/failopen/base.py:9-15,28-36`: while the breaker is open, `ensure_connection` raises `CircuitOpenError` (an `OperationalError`) on every query for the 30s cooldown (`data_stores.py:183-185`).
- `products/stamphog/backend/facade/api.py:112-125`: `has_reviewable_repo_config` is a plain `.exists()` query on that DB, so it raises during the outage.
- `products/review_hog/backend/api/settings.py:77-80`: `except Exception` maps that to `return False`; the serializer help_text at lines 50-54 documents False as "does not have at least one synced, enabled Stamphog repository".
- `products/review_hog/frontend/CodeReviewScene.tsx:1066-1067`: when `stamphog_connected` is false and the toggle is off, the disabledReason is literally "Connect a repository to Stamphog first. Stamphog is not set up for this project yet." There is no other frontend consumer of the flag that could disambiguate (grep over `products/review_hog/frontend/` shows only this line plus generated types).
So a project with a fully synced, enabled repo whose user has the toggle off sees a false "not set up yet" statement during any stamphog DB outage / breaker-open window (or any other DB error, e.g. connect timeout). The code comment at settings.py:73-76 explicitly anticipates this failure class.
votes.refutation: Attempted refutations: (1) The comment says the toggle "renders disabled until the read recovers", so the disabled state itself is intended, and during the outage the user could not act on the toggle anyway (the PATCH path would still succeed, but the celery consumer would find no repo config). This covers the disabled behavior but not the wording; the copy asserts a setup fact the backend cannot vouch for. (2) Blast radius is narrow: the scene is gated by the `review-hog` feature flag (`frontend/src/lib/constants.tsx:470`), the copy only shows when the toggle is already off (`CodeReviewScene.tsx:1066`), the window is one 30s breaker cooldown per outage, and it self-corrects with no persisted wrong state. (3) No test covers the fail-soft branch, so there is no precedent asserting the wording is intended for the failure case. None of these make the claim false; they only bound it to a minor, transient UX inaccuracy, which matches `consider` rather than should_fix.
